{{Quote|Curse you, Rebel! There's a thousand atmospheres out there! The hull can't stand much more. Let me fly this thing, or we're all dead men!|The Imperial, to Roark Garnet|<ref name="RPG" />}}
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Gender/Legends|male]] '''Imperial''' was part of the crew of a [[bathysphere]] operating in the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of a [[Unidentified Jovian planet|Jovian]] [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]]. At some point, he fought for control of the vessel with the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Roark Garnet/Legends|Roark Garnet]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|The repulsors. We're exposed to the planet's full gravity.|The Imperial|<ref name="RPG" />}}
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Gender/Legends|male]] member of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Imperial Military/Legends|Military]] was part of the crew of a [[bathysphere]]. The [[Unidentified bathysphere|bathysphere]] was assigned to operations under the cloud layer of a [[Unidentified Jovian planet|Jovian]] [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. At some point, the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Roark Garnet/Legends|Roark Garnet]] boarded the vessel. During an altercation in the control cabin&mdash;which also caused the bathysphere to spin out of control&mdash;Garnet dispatched the rest of the vessel's crew until only the Imperial remained. The two fought for control of the bathysphere as it plunged through the Jovian's cloud layers. During the struggle, the Imperial briefly got the upper hand on Garnet, taking control of the vessel, stabilizing the craft and arresting its descent. Moments later, Garnet took control of the bathysphere as the Imperial had exhausted himself trying to stabilize the stricken craft. The smuggler's intervention saved the bathysphere from colliding with a [[Unidentified flying life form|flying lifeform]] in the atmosphere, which the Imperial thought was impossible as he believed there were no life forms on the planet.<ref name="RPG" />

Shortly after, the craft's [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsors]] failed, exposing the bathysphere to the full force of the planet's gravity of a thousand atmospheres. The Imperial was of the opinion that he and Garnet were doomed, and lay on the deck. Garnet inquired where the ship's repulsors were; the Imperial indicated the location to the aft and the smuggler went and fixed them. With the danger averted, the Imperial decided that the temporary truce between him and Garnet was over. As the smuggler was returning to the control cabin, the Imperial switched the setting on his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]]. Garnet heard the click, and unsure if it was set to [[Stun/Legends|stun]] or [[Death/Legends|kill]], decided to act first, leaping through the door to the control cabin firing. The Imperial managed to get his own shot off after Garnet's first, but the smuggler dodged the blast.<ref name="RPG" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|We're doomed. Trapped on a gas giant beneath the cloud layer.|The Imperial's fatalistic view aboard the bathysphere after the repulsors stop working|<ref name="RPG" />}}
The Imperial was a competent individual, capable of taking control of the vessel he was assigned to in an emergency. He was also fatalistic, believing that the loss of the craft's repulsors meant that he was doomed to die and did not attempt to repair them himself. The Imperial was also willing to stun or kill Garnet, who had just saved his life by repairing the repulsors. He was also stunned by the appearance of a life form in the atmosphere of the Jovian gas giant, as he believed that no life forms existing on the planet.<ref name="RPG" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Imperial appeared in [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']], published by [[West End Games]] in [[1987]]. He was a non-player character used in an example scenario of how to perform opposed rolls&mdash;where a player character rolls against another player character or non-player character controlled by the gamemaster to determine the outcome of an action&mdash;during a game.<ref name="RPG" />
